Yes—under those conditions, you should be able to spot the Moon easily.

A **37% illuminated crescent**, **21° above the horizon**, in a **clear, fully dark sky** is conspicuous to normal unaided vision. Its distance of about **400,000 km** makes it only slightly smaller than average and does not meaningfully hinder visibility. At azimuth **238.6°**, look toward the **west-southwest**, roughly two fist-widths above the horizon.

Only a local obstruction—buildings, terrain, clouds, or severe haze/light scatter near the horizon—would make it impossible to see. Astronomically, it is definitely visible, so unfortunately it is not “impossible to see” at that moment.
